card.name: Verbs before expected 'be' in old prose
card.fires_on: Helper or linking verbs (deemed, will, may, would, could, to) in archaic or historical prose, where a passive or predicate phrase like 'be necessary' or 'expedient' comes next.

modes.label: Modal before 'be'
modes.description: A modal such as will, may, would or could right before 'be' plus an adjective like necessary or pleasing.
modes.example: it<< will>> be necessary to go back of them a

modes.label: Judgment verb
modes.description: A verb of judging or thinking, such as deemed or thought, before an adjective or 'it his duty'.
modes.example: it is<< deemed>> expedient to give plates, exhibiting the

modes.label: Infinitive 'to'
modes.description: The word 'to' introducing a verb in a formal historical sentence.
modes.example: enable our little navy<< to>> annoy in the utmost extent, the trade

card.plain: It fires on small verbs in old-style formal writing that lead into a phrase like 'be necessary' or 'deemed expedient'.
